extraction_notes.note: Equation (2) in the introduction repeats (3) (\label{2.1}) of Section 2; both are numbered, and the labelled copy that the paper cites is kept, against the 'else the first' tie-break, because the finishing step matches the node to the labelled fact. For (2.3)/(4.1), (2.4)/(4.5), (2.5)/(4.10) the first copy is kept.
Each sentence both derives a formula (by Lemma 1.1 of Pritchard-You) and introduces new kernels/coefficients used later; typed as definition rather than claim.
The defining sentence runs on with a comma straight into Theorem 4.6, so the node ends at a comma.
The concluding section lists vague future directions (cost functionals with Volterra kernels, delay-dependent consistency conditions) that were not stated precisely enough for open_problem nodes.

nodes.name: Equation (3)
nodes.statement: x_{i}(t) & = & \varphi(t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)x_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)x^{N}(s)ds\nonumber\\ & & +\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}(s)ds+ \int_{0}^{t}\sigma(t,s)dW_{i}(s).

nodes.name: Cost functional of agent i
nodes.statement: \mathcal{J}_{i}(u_{i},u_{-i})=\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left[ (x_{i}(t)-\gamma x^{N}(t)-\eta )^{2}+Ru_{i}^{2}(t)\right] dt,

nodes.name: Differential case state equation
nodes.statement: x_{i}(t)=x(0)+\int_{0}^{t}b(s)x_{i}(s)ds+ \int_{0}^{t}c(s)u_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma(s)dW_i(s).

nodes.name: SDE with delay in state
nodes.statement: dx_{i}(t)=\left[ A(t)x_{i}(t-h)+\int_{t-h}^{t}B(t,s)x_{i}(s)ds\right] dt+C(t)u_i(t)dt+D(t)dW_i(t),

nodes.name: SDE with delay in control
nodes.statement: dx_{i}(t)=A(t)x_{i}(t)dt+C(t)u_i(t-h)dt+D(t)dW_i(t),

nodes.name: Limiting state equation
nodes.statement: x_{i}(t)&=&\varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)x_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)a(s)ds\nonumber \\ &&+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}(s)ds+ \int_{0}^{t}\sigma(t,s)dW_{i}(s),\quad t\in[0,T],

nodes.name: Limiting cost functional
nodes.statement: \overline{J}_{i}(u_{i})=\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\Big[(x_{i}(t)-\gamma a(t)-\eta )^{2}+R|u_{i}(t)|^{2}\Big] dt.

nodes.name: Optimal control of limiting problem via BSVIE
nodes.statement: \overline{u}_{i}(t)=-\frac{1}{2R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\!\!\int_{t}^{T}c(s,t) \overline{y}_{i}(s)ds

nodes.name: Linear BSVIE for adjoint
nodes.statement: \overline{y}_{i}(t)=2\overline{x}_{i}(t)-2\gamma a(t)-2\eta +\int_{t}^{T}b(s,t)\overline{y}_{i}(s)ds-\int_{t}^{T}\overline{z} _{i}(t,s)dW_{i}(s),

nodes.name: Adjoint process via resolvent kernel
nodes.statement: \overline{y}_{i}(t)=2\overline{x}_{i}(t)-2\gamma a(t)-2\eta +\int_{t}^{T}2P(s,t)[\overline{x}_{i}(s)-\gamma a(s)-\eta ]ds,

nodes.name: Resolvent kernel series
nodes.statement: P(s,t) =\sum\limits_{k=1}^{\infty }\Lambda^{k}(s,t), \quad \Lambda^{1}(s,t) =b(s,t), \quad \Lambda^{k+1}(s,t)=\int_{t}^{s}b(s,r)\Lambda^{k}(r,t)dr.

nodes.name: Optimal control in terms of state
nodes.statement: \overline{u}_{i}(t)=-\frac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\!\!\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(s,t)[\overline{x}_{i}(s)-\gamma a(s)-\eta ]ds,

nodes.name: Kernel c-hat
nodes.statement: \widehat{c}(s,t)=c(s,t)+\int_{t}^{s}P(s,r)c(r,t)dr,\quad s\geq t.

nodes.name: Transformed limiting state equation
nodes.statement: x_{i}(t)=\widehat{\varphi }(t)+\widehat{\sigma }_i(t)+\int_0^t\widehat{f}(t,s)a(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)u_{i}(s)ds,

nodes.name: Transformed coefficients
nodes.statement: \widehat{\varphi }(t) &=\varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}P(t,s)\varphi(s)ds, \nonumber\\ \widehat{\sigma }_{i}(t) &=\int_{0}^{t}\left[\sigma(t,s)+\int_{s}^{t}P(t,r)\sigma(r,s)dr\right] dW_{i}(s),\nonumber\\ \widehat{f}(t,s)&=f(t,s)+\int_{s}^{t}P(t,r)f(r,s)dr.

nodes.name: Optimal state equation (stochastic Volterra-Fredholm)
nodes.statement: \overline{x}_{i}(t) = & \; \widehat{\varphi }(t)+\widehat{\sigma}_i (t)-\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{s\wedge t}\widehat{c}(t,r)\widehat{c} (s,r)\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{r}}\overline{x}_{i}(s)drds \nonumber\\ & + \int_0^t\widehat{f}(t,s)a(s)ds+\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{s\wedge t} \widehat{c}(t,r)\widehat{c}(s,r)dr\cdot[\gamma a(s)+\eta ]ds.

nodes.name: Fredholm equation for expected optimal state
nodes.statement: \mathbb{E}\overline{x}_{i}(t)=\widehat{\varphi }(t)+\int_0^t\widehat{f}(t,s)a(s)ds+\frac{1}{R} \int_{0}^{T}M(t,s)[\gamma a(s)+\eta-\mathbb{E}\overline{x}_{i}(s)]ds,

nodes.name: Kernel M
nodes.statement: M(t,s)=\int_{0}^{s\wedge t}\widehat{c}(t,r)\widehat{c}(s,r)dr,\quad t,s\in[0,T].

nodes.name: Fredholm integral equation
nodes.statement: x(t)=\psi (t)+\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}A(t,s)x(s)ds,\quad t\in[0,T],

nodes.name: Operator Gamma
nodes.statement: \lbrack \Gamma a](t)=\widehat{\varphi }(t)+\int_0^t\widehat{f}(t,s)a(s)ds +\frac{1}{R} \int_{0}^{T}M(t,s)\big\{\gamma a(s)+\eta-[\Gamma a](s)\big\}ds.

nodes.name: NCE equation
nodes.statement: \widehat{a}(t)=\widehat{\varphi}(t)+\int_0^t\widehat{f}(t,s) \widehat{a}(s)ds+\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}M(t,s)[(\gamma-1)\widehat{a}(s)+\eta ]ds,

nodes.name: NCE equation in Fredholm form
nodes.statement: \widehat{a}(t)=\widetilde{\varphi}(t)+\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}\widetilde{M}(t,s)[(\gamma -1)\widehat{a}(s)+\eta ]ds,

nodes.name: Coefficients of Fredholm NCE form
nodes.statement: \widetilde{\varphi}(t)&=\widehat{\varphi}(t)+\int_{0}^{t}\widetilde{P}(t,s)\widehat{\varphi} (s)ds, \nonumber \\ \widetilde{M}(t,s)&=M(t,s)+\int_{0}^{t}\widetilde{P}(t,r)M(r,s)dr,

nodes.name: Resolvent kernel P-tilde
nodes.statement: \widetilde{P}(t,s) = \sum\limits_{k=1}^{\infty }\widetilde{\Lambda}^{k}(t,s), \quad \widetilde{\Lambda}^{1}(t,s) =\widehat{f}(t,s), \quad \widetilde{\Lambda}^{k+1}(t,s)=\int_{s}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,r)\widetilde{\Lambda}^{k}(r,s)dr.

nodes.name: Decentralized control
nodes.statement: \widehat{u}_{i}(t)=-\frac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\!\!\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c} (s,t)[x_{i}(s)-\gamma \widehat{a}(s)-\eta]ds

nodes.name: Closed-loop state under decentralized control
nodes.statement: x_{i}(t)=& \; \widehat{\varphi }(t)+\widehat{\sigma }_i (t)+\int_0^t\widehat{f}(t,s)x^{N}(s)ds\nonumber\\ &- \int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)\frac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{s}}\!\!\int_{s}^{T}\widehat{c} (r,s)[x_{i}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta]drds,

nodes.name: Optimal state with NCE solution
nodes.statement: \overline{x}_{i}(t) = & \; \widehat{\varphi }(t)+\widehat{\sigma_i} (t)-\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{s\wedge t}\widehat{c}(t,r)\widehat{c} (s,r)\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{r}}\overline{x}_{i}(s)drds \nonumber \\ & +\int_0^t\widehat{f}(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds+\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{s\wedge t} \widehat{c}(t,r)\widehat{c}(s,r)dr\cdot \lbrack \gamma \widehat{a}(s)+\eta ]ds.

nodes.name: Stochastic Volterra-Fredholm equation (6.1)
nodes.statement: x(t)=\varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}A(t,s)x(s)ds-\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{s \wedge t}B(t,r)B(s,r)\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{r}}x(s)drds,

nodes.name: Smallness condition (6.2)
nodes.statement: T\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{s\wedge t}|\widehat{B} (t,r)B(s,r)|^{2}drdsdt<\frac{R^{2}}{3}.

nodes.name: B-hat and P_0 kernels (6.3)
nodes.statement: &&\widehat{B}(t,r)=B(t,r)+\int_{r}^{t}P_0(t,v)B(v,r)dv,\quad t,v\in[0,T],\nonumber\\ &&P_0(t,v) =\sum\limits_{k=1}^{\infty}\Lambda^{k}(t,v), \quad \Lambda^{1}(t,t) =A(t,v), \quad \Lambda^{k+1}(t,v)=\int_{v}^{t}A(t,r)\Lambda^{k}(r,v)dr .

nodes.statement: \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x(s)|^{2}ds\leq 6\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{\varphi}(s)|^{2}ds,

nodes.statement: x(t)=\varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}A(t,s)x(s)ds-\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{s \wedge t}B(t,r)B(s,r)\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{r}}y(s)drds,

nodes.statement: \mathbb{E}\int_0^T|\widehat{a}(s)-\overline{x}^{N}(s)|^2ds=O\Big(\frac{1}{N}\Big),

nodes.name: Mean field term (state average)
nodes.statement:
There exist a
collection of large number negligible players where individual state
follows linear stochastic differential equations

\begin{equation} dx_i(t)=\big[A_i x_i(t)+B_i u_i(t)+F_i x^{(N)}(t)\big]dt+D_idW_{i}(t),
 \end{equation}

where $x^{(N)}=\frac{1}{N}\sum\limits_{i=1}^{N}x_i$ denotes the
state average or mean
 field term.
nodes.statement_short: Classical mean-field LQG setup: agents follow linear SDEs coupled through the state average $x^{(N)}$.

nodes.name: Controlled stochastic Volterra integral system
nodes.statement:
Motivated by above concerns, in this paper, we consider the following controlled stochastic
Volterra integral equations

\begin{eqnarray} x_{i}(t)&=&\varphi(t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)x_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)x^{N}(s)ds\nonumber \\
&&+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}(s)ds+
\int_{0}^{t}\sigma(t,s)dW_{i}(s).
\end{eqnarray}

where $x^{N}=\frac{1}{N}\sum^{N}_{j=1}x_j$ is the mean field term
which characterizes average interaction and mass effects of our
population in \emph{spatial} variable, $\varphi,b,c,\sigma$ are
deterministic functions, called the kernels, which characterize path
dependence of out state in its \emph{temporal} variable.
nodes.statement_short: The model: each agent's state solves a controlled stochastic Volterra integral equation with mean field term $x^N$ and deterministic kernels.

nodes.name: Filtered probability space and Brownian motions
nodes.statement:
Suppose $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, (\mathcal{F}_t)_{0\leq t\leq T},
\mathbb{P})$ is a complete filtered probability space on which
$W(t)=(W_i(t))_{0 \leq t \leq T}$, $1\leq i\leq N$ are independent scalar-valued Brownian motions.

nodes.name: Natural filtration
nodes.statement:
It is also assumed $(\mathcal
F_t)_{0\leq t\leq T}$ is the natural filtration generated by $W(t)$
and $\mathcal F=\mathcal F_T$.

nodes.name: Function spaces L^2, L^2_F, C
nodes.statement_short: Spaces of square-integrable deterministic functions, square-integrable adapted processes, and continuous functions on $[0,T]$.

nodes.name: Large population of negligible players
nodes.statement:
Now consider the stochastic large population integral system which consists of $N$ individual negligible players, denote respectively
by $\mathcal{A}_i, i=1, 2, \cdots, N$.

nodes.name: Individual cost functional
nodes.statement:
All
individual players are coupled in terms of their individual cost functional
as follows:
\begin{equation} \mathcal{J}_{i}(u_{i},u_{-i})=\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left[
(x_{i}(t)-\gamma x^{N}(t)-\eta )^{2}+Ru_{i}^{2}(t)\right] dt,
\end{equation}
where $u_{-i}=(u_1,\cdots,u_{i-1},u_{i+1},\cdots,u_{N})$, and $R>0$,
$\gamma$, $\eta$ are constants.
nodes.statement_short: Quadratic tracking cost of agent $i$ penalizing deviation from $\gamma x^N+\eta$ plus control energy $Ru_i^2$.

nodes.name: Differential case
nodes.statement:
The first one is the differential case, i.e., the kernels $\varphi,b,c,\sigma $
are independent of $t.$ In this case, equation (\ref{2.1}) becomes the following
stochastic \emph{integral} equation,
\begin{eqnarray} x_{i}(t)=x(0)+\int_{0}^{t}b(s)x_{i}(s)ds+
\int_{0}^{t}c(s)u_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma(s)dW_i(s).
\end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Kernels independent of $t$ reduce the Volterra system to a linear SDE in integral form.

nodes.name: SDE with delay in state
nodes.statement:
The second case is the
stochastic differential equation with delay in state which can be
described as
\begin{equation} dx_{i}(t)=\left[
A(t)x_{i}(t-h)+\int_{t-h}^{t}B(t,s)x_{i}(s)ds\right]
dt+C(t)u_i(t)dt+D(t)dW_i(t),
\end{equation}
where $h>0$ is the delay or lag parameter, $x_{i}(t)=k(t),$ $t\in \lbrack -h,0].$

nodes.name: SDE with delay in control
nodes.statement:
The third one
includes stochastic differential equations with delay in control
variable which evolves as
\begin{equation} dx_{i}(t)=A(t)x_{i}(t)dt+C(t)u_i(t-h)dt+D(t)dW_i(t),
\end{equation}
where $h>0,$ $x_{i}(t)=k(t),$ $t\in \lbrack -h,0].$

nodes.name: Delayed SDEs as stochastic Volterra equations
nodes.statement:
Under certain
conditions, we can transform equation (\ref{2.4}) and (\ref{2.5})
into the following form of stochastic Volterra integral equation,
\[
x_{i}(t)=\psi(t)+\int_{0}^{t}K(t,s)u_i(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\Phi
(t,s)D(s)dW_i(s).
\]
assumptions:
Under certain
conditions
conclusions:
we can transform equation (\ref{2.4}) and (\ref{2.5})
into the following form of stochastic Volterra integral equation
nodes.statement_short: Delay-in-state and delay-in-control SDEs can be rewritten as stochastic Volterra integral equations.

nodes.name: Deterministic approximation a(t) of the state average
nodes.statement:
First, let us formulate one auxiliary limiting control problem via
the approximation of state average $x^{N}$ by some deterministic
function $a(t)$.

nodes.name: Auxiliary limiting control problem
nodes.statement:
Now we introduce the following state
equation

\begin{eqnarray} x_{i}(t)&=&\varphi
(t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)x_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)a(s)ds\nonumber
\\
&&+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}(s)ds+
\int_{0}^{t}\sigma(t,s)dW_{i}(s),\quad t\in[0,T],
\end{eqnarray}

and the cost functional for player $\mathcal{A}_i$
($i=1,2,\cdots,N$),

\begin{eqnarray} \overline{J}_{i}(u_{i})=\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\Big[(x_{i}(t)-\gamma a(t)-\eta )^{2}+R|u_{i}(t)|^{2}\Big] dt.
\end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Single-agent LQ control of a Volterra state where the mean field is frozen to a deterministic $a(\cdot)$.

nodes.name: Optimal control of the limiting problem via BSVIE
nodes.statement:
In this case, it follows from \cite{S-W-Y 2013} or \cite{Y 2008} that the optimal control $\overline{u}_{i}$ can be
represented by

\begin{equation} \overline{u}_{i}(t)=-\frac{1}{2R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\!\!\int_{t}^{T}c(s,t)
\overline{y}_{i}(s)ds
\end{equation}

where $\overline{y}_i$ satisfies the following linear Backward Stochastic Volterra Integral Equation (BSVIE)

\begin{equation} \overline{y}_{i}(t)=2\overline{x}_{i}(t)-2\gamma a(t)-2\eta
+\int_{t}^{T}b(s,t)\overline{y}_{i}(s)ds-\int_{t}^{T}\overline{z}
_{i}(t,s)dW_{i}(s),
\end{equation}

and $\overline{x}_{i}$ is the solution of (\ref{3.1}) with respect
to $\overline{u}_i$.

to $\overline{u}_i$
conclusions:
the optimal control $\overline{u}_{i}$ can be

nodes.statement_short: The optimal control of the limiting problem is a conditional expectation of an integral of the adjoint BSVIE solution.

nodes.name: Resolvent kernel P
nodes.statement:
Due to the special form of (\ref{3.4}), by using Lemma 1.1 in \cite{Y 1996} we can formulate $\overline{y}_{i}$ as

\begin{equation} \overline{y}_{i}(t)=2\overline{x}_{i}(t)-2\gamma a(t)-2\eta
+\int_{t}^{T}2P(s,t)[\overline{x}_{i}(s)-\gamma a(s)-\eta ]ds,
\end{equation}

where for any $0\leq t\leq s\leq T,$

\begin{eqnarray} P(s,t) =\sum\limits_{k=1}^{\infty }\Lambda^{k}(s,t), \quad
\Lambda^{1}(s,t) =b(s,t), \quad
\Lambda^{k+1}(s,t)=\int_{t}^{s}b(s,r)\Lambda^{k}(r,t)dr.
\end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: The BSVIE solution is written explicitly through the resolvent kernel $P=\sum_k\Lambda^k$ of $b$ (Lemma 1.1 of Pritchard-You).

nodes.name: Remark 3.1 (resolvent kernel bounds)
nodes.statement: Note that (\ref{3.5}) can be viewed as a constant variation formula in our setup and $P$ is called ``resolvent kernel". In the special multi-dimensional differential case, $P$ becomes the solution of fundamental matrix. The method of infinite series will be frequently adopted in our following analysis. On the other hand, it is straightforward to verify \[ |\Lambda^{k}(s,t)|<\frac{M^{k}|t-s|^{k-1}}{(k-1)!},\quad t,s\in[0,T],\quad k\geq 1, \] where $M$ is the upper bound of $b$, thus $P$ is bounded. Moreover, if $b$ is continuous in $t,$ then one can see that $P$ is also continuous in $t.$
nodes.statement_short: (3.5) is a variation-of-constants formula; the iterated kernels obey factorial bounds so $P$ is bounded, and continuous if $b$ is.
nodes.label: remark3.1

nodes.name: Kernel c-hat
nodes.statement:
Substituting (\ref{3.5}) into (\ref{3.3}), we can rewrite the
optimal control in (\ref{3.3}) as

\begin{equation} \overline{u}_{i}(t)=-\frac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\!\!\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(s,t)[\overline{x}_{i}(s)-\gamma a(s)-\eta ]ds,
\end{equation}

where

\begin{eqnarray} \widehat{c}(s,t)=c(s,t)+\int_{t}^{s}P(s,r)c(r,t)dr,\quad s\geq t.
\end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Optimal control in feedback-on-future-path form with the modified kernel $\widehat c=c+\int P c$.

nodes.name: Continuity of c-hat
nodes.statement:
Note that if $b$, $c$ are continuous in $t,$ by using Remark \ref{remark3.1} one can see that $\widehat{c}
(t,s)$ is also continuous in $t.$
assumptions: $b$, $c$ are continuous in $t,$
conclusions:
$\widehat{c}
(t,s)$ is also continuous in $t.$

nodes.name: Transformed coefficients phi-hat, sigma-hat, f-hat
nodes.statement:
On the other hand, by using Lemma
1.1. of \cite{Y 1996}, we can rewrite (\ref{3.1}) as

\begin{equation} x_{i}(t)=\widehat{\varphi }(t)+\widehat{\sigma }_i(t)+\int_0^t\widehat{f}(t,s)a(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)u_{i}(s)ds,
\end{equation}

where $P$ is defined in (\ref{3.5.1}) and

\begin{align} \widehat{\varphi }(t) &=\varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}P(t,s)\varphi(s)ds, \nonumber\\
\widehat{\sigma }_{i}(t) &=\int_{0}^{t}\left[\sigma(t,s)+\int_{s}^{t}P(t,r)\sigma(r,s)dr\right] dW_{i}(s),\nonumber\\
\widehat{f}(t,s)&=f(t,s)+\int_{s}^{t}P(t,r)f(r,s)dr.
\end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Eliminating the $b$-term via the resolvent kernel gives the state in explicit form with coefficients $\widehat\varphi,\widehat\sigma_i,\widehat f$.

nodes.name: Kernel M
nodes.statement_short: The mean of the optimal state solves a Fredholm equation with kernel $M(t,s)=\int_0^{s\wedge t}\widehat c\widehat c$.

nodes.name: Solvability of Fredholm integral equation
nodes.statement: Consider the following Fredholm integral equation \begin{equation} x(t)=\psi (t)+\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}A(t,s)x(s)ds,\quad t\in[0,T], \end{equation} where $\psi $, $A$ are bounded and continuous functions in $t$. If \[ \sup_{t\in [0,T]}\int_{0}^{T}|A(t,s)|^{2}ds<R, \quad \sup_{t\in [0,T]}|\psi (t)|^{2}<\infty , \] then there exists a unique continuous solution $x(\cdot)$ of (\ref{3.12}).
assumptions: $\psi $, $A$ are bounded and continuous functions in $t$
\sup_{t\in [0,T]}\int_{0}^{T}|A(t,s)|^{2}ds<R, \quad \sup_{t\in [0,T]}|\psi (t)|^{2}<\infty ,
conclusions: there exists a unique continuous solution $x(\cdot)$ of (\ref{3.12}).
nodes.statement_short: A Fredholm equation with $L^2$-small kernel ($<R$) has a unique continuous solution.
nodes.label: lemma-1

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.1
nodes.statement: From Lemma \ref{lemma-1}, we can get the following result directly.
nodes.statement_short: Direct application of Lemma 3.1 to the Fredholm equation (3.10).

nodes.name: Solvability of the expected optimal state equation
nodes.statement: Suppose $\varphi,$ $b$, $f$, $c$ are bounded and continuous in $t$ such that \[ \sup_{t\in \lbrack 0,T]}\int_{0}^{T}|M(t,s)|^{2}ds<R. \] Then, given $a\in C[0,T]$, there exists a unique continuous function $\mathbb{E} \overline{x}_i(\cdot)$ satisfying equation (\ref{3.10}).
assumptions: $\varphi,$ $b$, $f$, $c$ are bounded and continuous in $t$
\sup_{t\in \lbrack 0,T]}\int_{0}^{T}|M(t,s)|^{2}ds<R.
given $a\in C[0,T]$
conclusions: there exists a unique continuous function $\mathbb{E} \overline{x}_i(\cdot)$ satisfying equation (\ref{3.10}).
nodes.statement_short: For each continuous $a$, the mean optimal state is the unique continuous solution of (3.10).
nodes.label: theorem-1

nodes.name: Operator Gamma
Nash certainty equivalence (NCE) equation
nodes.statement:
The Nash certainty equivalence (NCE) equation in our setting is thus
\begin{equation} \widehat{a}(t)=\widehat{\varphi}(t)+\int_0^t\widehat{f}(t,s)
\widehat{a}(s)ds+\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}M(t,s)[(\gamma-1)\widehat{a}(s)+\eta ]ds,
\end{equation}
where $\widehat{a}$ is the corresponding solution.
nodes.statement_short: The consistency (fixed-point) condition $a=\Gamma a$ written as a deterministic Volterra-Fredholm equation for $\widehat a$.

nodes.name: Fredholm form of the NCE equation
nodes.statement_short: Removing the Volterra part via the resolvent $\widetilde P$ of $\widehat f$ turns the NCE equation into a Fredholm equation.

nodes.name: Existence and uniqueness for the NCE equation
nodes.statement: Suppose $\varphi,b,c,f$ are bounded and continuous in $t.$ If \[ \sup_{t\in [0,T]}\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert (\gamma-1)\widetilde{M}(t,s)\right\vert ^{2}ds<R, \] then (\ref{3.14}) admits a unique solution $a \in C[0,T]$.
assumptions: $\varphi,b,c,f$ are bounded and continuous in $t.$
\sup_{t\in [0,T]}\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert (\gamma-1)\widetilde{M}(t,s)\right\vert ^{2}ds<R,
conclusions: (\ref{3.14}) admits a unique solution $a \in C[0,T]$.
nodes.statement_short: Under an $L^2$ smallness condition on $(\gamma-1)\widetilde M$, the NCE equation has a unique continuous solution.

nodes.name: Remarks on the optimal control, optimal state and NCE equation
nodes.statement:
Before concluding this section, let us make some remarks on
(\ref{3.6}), (\ref{3.9}) and (\ref{3.14}). Firstly, note that $\overline{u}_i(t)$ depends on the path of $\overline{x}_i$ in
$[t,T]$. Moreover, $\widehat{c}$ is a general non-separable function
of $(t,s)$. In particular, such a general feature can naturally
degenerate and transform into the form with Riccati equation
involved, see Section 4.1 below. Secondly, equation (\ref{3.9}) is a
new type of stochastic equation with double integrals, which is
essentially different from the corresponding equation in stochastic differential equations (SDEs) case.
Since it has both the characters of Volterra and Fredholm equation,
we then call it a stochastic Volterra-Fredholm equation. We will
study its solvability under certain conditions in next section by noting our main concern here is NCE equation. Thirdly, we express the NCE
equation in our setting by means of deterministic Volterra-Fredholm
equation. This idea is also different to other literature on SDEs.
nodes.statement_short: The control depends on the future path; (3.9) is a new stochastic Volterra-Fredholm equation; the NCE equation is a deterministic Volterra-Fredholm equation.

nodes.name: Stochastic Volterra-Fredholm equation
nodes.statement:
Secondly, equation (\ref{3.9}) is a
new type of stochastic equation with double integrals, which is
essentially different from the corresponding equation in stochastic differential equations (SDEs) case.
Since it has both the characters of Volterra and Fredholm equation,
we then call it a stochastic Volterra-Fredholm equation.

nodes.name: epsilon-Nash equilibrium
nodes.statement: Given a set of controls $\widehat{u}_i\in L^2_{\mathcal{F}}(0,T;\mathbb{R})$ with $i=1,2,\cdots,N$, if for any $i$, $1\leq i\leq N,$ $\mathcal{J}_i(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})\leq \mathcal{J}_i(u_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})+\epsilon, $ where $\epsilon>0$, $\widehat{u}_{-i}=(\widehat{u}_1,\cdots,\widehat{u}_{i-1},\widehat{u}_{i+1},\cdots,\widehat{u}_{N})$, $u_i\in L^2_{\mathcal{F}}(0,T;\mathbb{R})$, then we call this set of controls $\widehat{u}_i$, $1\leq i\leq N$ an $\epsilon$-Nash equilibrium with respect to costs $\mathcal{J}_i$ with $1\leq i\leq N$.

nodes.name: Decentralized control
nodes.statement:
Suppose $\widehat{a}$ is the solution of NCE equation (\ref{3.14}), then we can
define the decentralized control $\widehat{u}_i$ for agent $\mathcal{A}_i$ as
follows:

\begin{equation} \widehat{u}_{i}(t)=-\frac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\!\!\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}
(s,t)[x_{i}(s)-\gamma \widehat{a}(s)-\eta]ds
\end{equation}

where $x_i$ is the solution of (\ref{2.1}) corresponding to
$\widehat{u}_i$.
nodes.statement_short: Each agent uses the limiting-problem feedback with $a$ replaced by the NCE solution $\widehat a$, applied to its true state.

nodes.name: Generic constant C
nodes.statement:
In the following, we denote by $C$ a generic
positive constant independent of $N$ that may change from line to
line.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.2
nodes.statement: Given $y(\cdot )\in L_{\mathcal{F}}^{2}(0,T;\mathbb{R}),$ consider the following Volterra equation \begin{eqnarray} x(t)=\varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}A(t,s)x(s)ds-\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{s \wedge t}B(t,r)B(s,r)\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{r}}y(s)drds, \end{eqnarray} which obviously admits a unique solution $x(\cdot)$ under above assumptions. nodes.statement_short: Contraction mapping: freeze the Fredholm term, solve the Volterra equation via the resolvent, then apply Lemma 3.1.

nodes.name: Remark 3.2 (on the conditions of Lemma 3.2)
nodes.statement: Some comment to (\ref{6.1}). To be shown later, it plays some key role in our remaining analysis. Since our first concern here is the solvability of (\ref{6.1}) under certain conditions. In such sense, we do not pursue the most general assumptions here and we hope to weaken these conditions in our future work.

nodes.name: Mean-field approximation for the optimal states
nodes.statement: Suppose NCE equation (\ref{3.14}) admits a unique solution $\widehat{a}(\cdot)$, and (\ref{6.2}), (\ref{6.3}) hold with $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c}$, then \begin{eqnarray} \mathbb{E}\int_0^T|\widehat{a}(s)-\overline{x}^{N}(s)|^2ds=O\Big(\frac{1}{N}\Big), \end{eqnarray} where $\overline{x}^{N}(t)=\frac{1}{N}\sum\limits_{i=1}^{N}\overline{x}_{i}(t)$ and $\overline{x}_i$ satisfies (\ref{3.20}).
assumptions: NCE equation (\ref{3.14}) admits a unique solution $\widehat{a}(\cdot)$
(\ref{6.2}), (\ref{6.3}) hold with $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c}$,
conclusions: \mathbb{E}\int_0^T|\widehat{a}(s)-\overline{x}^{N}(s)|^2ds=O\Big(\frac{1}{N}\Big),
nodes.statement_short: The average of the limiting optimal states is $O(1/N)$-close in mean square to the NCE solution.
nodes.label: lemma-2

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.3
nodes.statement: From (\ref{3.14}) and (\ref{3.20}), we know the difference between $\overline{x}_i$ and $\widehat{a}$ satisfies the type of Equation (\ref{6.1}) with $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c}$, $\varphi=\widehat{\sigma}_i$. Then by means of (\ref{6.4}), \begin{eqnarray*} \mathbb{E}\int_0^T|\overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt &\leq &C\mathbb{E}\int_0^T\left\vert \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^{N}\widehat{\sigma }_{i}(t)\right\vert ^{2}dt. \end{eqnarray*} It then follows from the boundedness of $\sigma$ and $P$ in (\ref{3.8.1}), together with the independence of $W_i$ ($i=1,2,\cdots,N$) that \[ \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt=O\left(\frac{1}{N}\right), \] which implies the desired result. \hfill
nodes.statement_short: The difference solves (6.1) with $\varphi=\widehat\sigma_i$; apply (6.4) and independence of the $W_i$.

nodes.name: Mean-field approximation for the closed-loop states
nodes.statement: Suppose NCE equation (\ref{3.14}) admits a solution $\widehat{a}$, (\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for two cases of $A=\widehat{f}$, $B=\widehat{c},$ and $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c}$, then \begin{eqnarray} \mathbb{E}\int_0^T|\widehat{a}(s)-x^{N}(s)|^2ds+\sup\limits_{1\leq i\leq N}\mathbb{E}\int_0^T|x_i(t)-\overline{x}_i(t)|^2dt=O\Big(\frac 1 N\Big) \end{eqnarray} where $x^{N}(t)=\frac{1}{N}\sum\limits_{i=1}^{N}x_{i}(t),$ $x_i$ satisfies (\ref{3.19}).
assumptions: NCE equation (\ref{3.14}) admits a solution $\widehat{a}$,
(\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for two cases of $A=\widehat{f}$, $B=\widehat{c},$ and $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c}$,
conclusions: \mathbb{E}\int_0^T|\widehat{a}(s)-x^{N}(s)|^2ds+\sup\limits_{1\leq i\leq N}\mathbb{E}\int_0^T|x_i(t)-\overline{x}_i(t)|^2dt=O\Big(\frac 1 N\Big)
nodes.statement_short: Under decentralized controls, the population average is $O(1/N)$-close to $\widehat a$ and each state to its limiting counterpart.
nodes.label: lemma-3

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.4
nodes.statement: Comparing (\ref{3.19}) and (\ref{3.20}), we can rewrite $x_i(t)$ as \begin{align*} x_i(t)=& \; \overline{x}_i(t)+\int_0^t\widehat{f}(t,s)\Big[x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)\Big]ds \\ &-\frac{1}{R}\int_0^T\int_0^{s\wedge t}\widehat{c}(t,r)\widehat{c}(s,r)\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_r}[x_i(s)-\overline{x}_i(s)]drds. \end{align*} Therefore, \begin{align*} x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)=& \; \overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)+\int_0^t\widehat{f}(t,s)\Big[x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)\Big]ds\nonumber\\ & - \frac 1 R \int_0^T\int_0^{s\wedge t}\widehat{c}(t,r)\widehat{c}(s,r)\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_r}[x^N(s)-\widehat{a}(s)]drds\nonumber\\ &+\frac 1 R \int_0^T\int_0^{s\wedge t}\widehat{c}(t,r)\widehat{c}(s,r)\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_r}[\overline{x}^N(s)-\widehat{a}(s)]drds. \end{align*} By using Lemma \ref{lemma6-1}, Lemma \ref{lemma-2}, together with the boundedness of $\widehat{f}$ and $\widehat{c}$, we can obtain the desired result (\ref{3.23}). \hfill
nodes.statement_short: Write $x^N-\widehat a$ as a solution of (6.1) driven by $\overline x^N-\widehat a$, then apply Lemmas 3.2 and 3.3.

nodes.name: Cost approximation by the limiting problem
nodes.statement: Suppose $\varphi$, $f$, $b$ and $c$ are bounded and continuous in $t$, NCE equation (\ref{3.14}) admits a unique continuous solution $\widehat{a}\in C[0,T]$, $\overline{u}_i$ is the optimal control with state equation (\ref{3.1}), cost functional (\ref{3.2}) that is parameterized by $\widehat{a}$, (\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for two cases of $A=\widehat{f}$, $B=\widehat{c},$ and $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c}$. Then for $1\leq i\leq N$, we have \begin{eqnarray} \mid\mathcal{J}_i(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})-\overline{J}_i(\overline{u}_i)\mid=O\left(\frac {1} {\sqrt{N}}\right). \end{eqnarray}
assumptions: $\varphi$, $f$, $b$ and $c$ are bounded and continuous in $t$
NCE equation (\ref{3.14}) admits a unique continuous solution $\widehat{a}\in C[0,T]$
$\overline{u}_i$ is the optimal control with state equation (\ref{3.1}), cost functional (\ref{3.2}) that is parameterized by $\widehat{a}$
(\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for two cases of $A=\widehat{f}$, $B=\widehat{c},$ and $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c}$.
conclusions: \mid\mathcal{J}_i(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})-\overline{J}_i(\overline{u}_i)\mid=O\left(\frac {1} {\sqrt{N}}\right).
nodes.statement_short: Each agent's cost under the decentralized controls is within $O(1/\sqrt N)$ of the limiting optimal cost.
nodes.label: theorem3.2

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.3
nodes.statement: First from the definition of $\mathcal{J}_i$ in (\ref{2.2}) and $\overline{J}_i$ in (\ref{3.2}), \begin{align*} \mathcal{J}_{i}(\widehat{u}_{i},\widehat{u}_{-i})-\overline{J}_{i}( \overline{u}_{i}) \leq & \; C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert R|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}-R|\overline{u} _{i}(t)|^{2}\right\vert dt \\ &+C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert |x_{i}(t)-\gamma x^{N}(t)-\eta |^{2}-|\overline{ x}_{i}(t)-\gamma \widehat{a}(t)-\eta |^{2}\right\vert dt \\ \leq & \; C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}R\left[ |\widehat{u}_{i}(t)-\overline{u} _{i}(t)|^{2}+2|\overline{u}_{i}(t)|\cdot|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)-\overline{u} _{i}(t)|\right] dt \\ &+C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)-\overline{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma (x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a} (t))|^{2}dt \\ &+C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma \widehat{a}(t)-\eta |\cdot |x_{i}(t)-\overline{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma (x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t))|dt, \end{align*} where $x_{i}$ and $\overline{x}_{i}$ satisfy (\ref{3.19}) and (\ref{3.20}) respectively. It follows from (\ref{3.3}) and (\ref{3.18}) that \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)-\overline{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt \leq & \; \frac{1}{R^{2}}\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\left\vert \int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(s,t)[x_{i}(s)-\overline{x}_{i}(s)]ds\right\vert ^{2}dt \\ \leq & \; C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(s)-\overline{x}_{i}(s)|^{2}ds. \end{align*} Note that equation (\ref{3.20}) is one special case of (\ref{6.1}) with $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c}$. Under above requirement, then from inequality (\ref{6.4}) above we have the boundedness of $\overline{x}_i$ in $L^2_{\mathcal{F}}(0,T;\mathbb{R})$. Recalling (\ref{3.6}) with $a=\widehat{a}$, we can also get similar boundedness result for $\overline{u}_i$. As a result, by Schwarz's inequality, \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{u}_{i}(t)||\widehat{u}_{i}(t)-\overline{u}_{i}(t)|dt \leq & \left[ \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt\right] ^{\frac{1}{2}} \left[\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)-\overline{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt\right] ^{\frac{1}{2}} \\ \leq & \; C\left[ \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(s)-\overline{x}_{i}(s)|^{2}ds\right] ^{\frac{1}{2}}. \end{align*} On the other hand, \begin{eqnarray*} \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)-\overline{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma (x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t))|^{2}dt \leq C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)-\overline{x}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt+C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt. \end{eqnarray*} Similarly, we can use Schwarz's inequality to estimate \begin{eqnarray*} &&\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma \widehat{a}(t)-\eta |\cdot |x_{i}(t)-\overline{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma (x^{(N)}(t)-\widehat{a}(t))|dt\\ &&\leq C\left[\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)-\overline{x}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt\right]^{\frac 1 2}+C\left[\mathbb{E} \int_{0}^{T}|x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt\right]^{\frac 1 2}. \end{eqnarray*} Therefore, by using Lemma \ref{lemma-3}, we obtain the desired result. \hfill
nodes.statement_short: Expand the cost difference and bound each term by Schwarz's inequality via $\|x_i-\overline x_i\|$ and $\|x^N-\widehat a\|$. The key step is Lemma 3.4's $O(1/N)$ mean-square estimate.

nodes.name: Perturbation sizes epsilon_a, epsilon_b
nodes.statement:
In the following part, given two processes $\xi _{a}$, $\xi _{b}$ in $L^2_{\mathcal{F}}(0,T;\mathbb{R})$, we denote by
 
\begin{eqnarray} \epsilon _{a}=\left( \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\xi _{a}(t)|^{2}dt\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}<\infty , \quad
\epsilon _{b}=\left( \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\xi _{b}(t)|^{2}dt\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}<\infty .
\end{eqnarray}

nodes.name: Perturbed limiting control problem
nodes.statement:
For
comparison, we also discuss one perturbed version with state
equation

\begin{align}
x_{i}(t) = & \;\varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)x_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)
\widehat{a}(s)ds \nonumber \\
&+\int_{0}^{t}g(t,s)\xi
_{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma
(t,s)dW_{i}(s), \end{align}

and the cost functional
\[
J_{i}^{\xi }(u_{i})=\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left[ |x_{i}(t)-\gamma
\widehat{a}(t)-\eta +\xi _{b}(t)|^{2}+R|u_{i}(t)|^{2}\right]dt.
\]
Here $g$ is bounded deterministic function.
nodes.statement_short: Limiting control problem perturbed by $\xi_a$ in the dynamics and $\xi_b$ in the cost.

nodes.name: Lower bound for the perturbed cost
nodes.statement: Suppose $\overline{u}_{i}$ is an optimal control given in (\ref{3.6}) and \begin{eqnarray} \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)|^{2}dt+\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|u_{i}(t)|^{2}dt\leq C_{0}. \end{eqnarray} where $ x_{i},$ $u_{i}$ are defined in (\ref{6.7}), $C_{0}$ is a fixed constant. Moreover, $\widehat{a}$ is continuous and bounded, (\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c},$ then we have \[ J_{i}^{\xi }(u_{i})\geq \overline{J}_{i}(\overline{u}_{i})-C(1+\epsilon_b)(\epsilon_a+\epsilon_b). \]
assumptions: $\overline{u}_{i}$ is an optimal control given in (\ref{3.6})
$\widehat{a}$ is continuous and bounded,
(\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c},$
conclusions: J_{i}^{\xi }(u_{i})\geq \overline{J}_{i}(\overline{u}_{i})-C(1+\epsilon_b)(\epsilon_a+\epsilon_b).
nodes.statement_short: Perturbing dynamics and cost by $\xi_a,\xi_b$ lowers the attainable cost by at most $C(1+\epsilon_b)(\epsilon_a+\epsilon_b)$.
nodes.label: lemma6.2

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.5
nodes.statement: For convenience, we can rewrite (\ref{6.7}) as \begin{align*} x_{i}(t) = & \; \varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)x_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}^{\prime }(s)ds \\ &+\int_{0}^{t}g(t,s)\xi _{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)\overline{u}_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma (t,s)dW_{i}(s). \end{align*} Here $u_{i}^{\prime }(s)=u_{i}(s)-\overline{u}_{i}(s),$ \[ \overline{u}_{i}(s)=-\frac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c} (r,t)[x_{i}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]dr, \] where $x_{i}$ satisfies (\ref{6.7}), $\widehat{c}$ is given in (\ref{3.7}). It then follows from inequality (\ref{6.8}) that $\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|u_{i}^{\prime }(t)|^{2}dt\leq C$. Next we construct one auxiliary optimal control problem with state equation and cost functional as \begin{align} \widetilde{x}_{i}(t) = & \; \varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)\widetilde{x}_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds \nonumber \\ &+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}''(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)\overline{u}_{i}(s,\widetilde{x}_{i})ds+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma (t,s)dW_{i}(s), \end{align} and \[ \widetilde{J}_{i}(u_{i}'')=\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left[|\widetilde{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma \widehat{a}(t)-\eta |^{2}+R|u_{i}''(t)+\overline{u}_{i}(t,\widetilde{x}_{i})|^{2}\right]dt. \] where $u''_{i}$ is the control variable. For $t\in[0,T]$, $\overline{u}_{i}(t,\widetilde{x}_{i})$ in (\ref{6.9}) is defined as \[ \overline{u}_{i}(t,\widetilde{x}_{i})=-\frac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\!\!\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)[\widetilde{x}_{i}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]dr. \] Obviously, $\widetilde{J}_{i}(u_{i}'')$ attains its minimum when $u_{i}''=0,$ and the corresponding cost functional equals to $ \overline{J}_{i}(\overline{u}_{i}).$ On the other hand, by Lemma \ref{lemma6-1}, \[ M_{i}'(t)=\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}'(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)M_{i}'(s)ds-\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)M_{i}'(r)drds \] admits a unique solution $M_{i}'$ such that \[ \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|M_{i}^{\prime }(t)|^{2}dt\leq 6\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}'(s)ds\right\vert^{2}dt\leq C. \] If we take $u_{i}''=u_{i}'(s)=u_{i}(s)-\overline{u}_{i}(s)$, and $\widetilde{x}_{i}'$ is the corresponding solution of (\ref{6.9}), then $\widetilde{x}_{i}'=\overline{x}_{i}(t)+M_{i}'(t),$ where $\overline{x}_{i}(t)$ is the optimal state in (\ref{3.9}) with $a=\widehat{a}$. Moreover, recalling the boundedness of $\overline{x}_i$ in $L^2_{\mathcal{F}}(0,T;\mathbb{R})$, we also have $\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widetilde{x}_{i}'(t)|^{2}dt\leq C$. Since $x_{i}$ and $\widetilde{x}_{i}'$ are given in (\ref{6.7}) and (\ref{6.9}), thus their difference $d_{i}=x_{i}-\widetilde{x}_{i}'$ satisfy \[ d_{i}(t)=\int_{0}^{t}g(t,s)\xi _{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)d_{i}(s)ds-\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\!\!\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)d_{i}(r)drds. \] Under above requirements, from Lemma \ref{lemma6-1}, we have \[ \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)-\widetilde{x}_{i}^{\prime }(t)|^{2}dt\leq 6\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert\int_{0}^{t}g(t,s)\xi _{a}(s)ds\right\vert^{2}dt\leq C\epsilon _{a}^{2}. \] Following the similar arguments in \cite{N-H 2012}, we should have \[ |J_{i}^{\xi}(u_{i})-\widetilde{J}_{i}(u_{i}')| \leq C(1+\epsilon_b)(\epsilon _{a}+\epsilon _{b}), \] where $C$ does not depend on $\xi_a$ and $\xi_b$. After combining the estimate of $\widetilde{J}_{i}(u_{i}')\geq \overline{J}_i(\overline{u}_i)$, we can get the desired result. \hfill
nodes.statement_short: Construct an auxiliary control problem minimized at $u''=0$, compare states via Lemma 3.2, and bound cost differences as in Nguyen-Huang.

nodes.name: Uniform boundedness of the decentralized costs
nodes.statement: Suppose $\widehat{a}$ is solution of NCE equation (\ref{3.14}), (\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for two cases of $A=\widehat{f}$, $B=\widehat{c}$, and $A=0$, $B=\widehat{c}$. Then $\mathcal{J}_{i}(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})\leq C$, where $C$ does not depend on $N$.
assumptions: $\widehat{a}$ is solution of NCE equation (\ref{3.14}),
(\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for two cases of $A=\widehat{f}$, $B=\widehat{c}$, and $A=0$, $B=\widehat{c}$.
conclusions: $\mathcal{J}_{i}(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})\leq C$, where $C$ does not depend on $N$.
nodes.statement_short: The cost of each agent under the decentralized controls is bounded uniformly in $N$.
nodes.label: lemma6.3

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.6
nodes.statement: If we can prove \[ \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(s)|^{2}ds\leq C,\quad \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(s)|^{2}ds\leq C, \] where $x_i$ satisfies (\ref{3.19}), $C$ does not depend on $N,$ then the result holds directly. From (\ref{3.19}), we have \begin{align} x^{N}(t) = & \; \widehat{\varphi }(t)+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)x^{N}(s)ds+\frac{1}{N}\sum_{l=1}^{N}\widehat{\sigma }_{l}(t) \nonumber \\ &-\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)\frac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}s}\int_{s}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,s)[x^{N}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]drds, \end{align} where $x^{N}(t)=\frac{1}{N}\sum\limits_{l=1}^{N}x_{l}(t).$ Note that (\ref{6.10}) is one special case of equation (\ref{6.1}), (\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for $A=\widehat{f}$, $B=\widehat{c}$, it then follows from Lemma \ref{lemma6-1} that \begin{align} \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x^{N}(s)|^{2}ds \leq & \; C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{\varphi}(s)|^{2}ds+C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert \frac{1}{N}\sum_{l=1}^{N}\widehat{\sigma}_{l}(t)\right\vert ^{2}dt \nonumber \\ & +C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{a}(s)|^{2}ds+C. \end{align} As to $x_i$ in equation (\ref{3.19}), using (\ref{6.11}) and conditions (\ref{6.2}), (\ref{6.3}) with $A=0$, $B=\widehat{c}$, we should have $\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(s)|^{2}ds\leq C$ where $C$ is independent of $N$. At last, we know that \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt = & \; \frac{1}{R^{2}}\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)[x_{i}(r)-\gamma\widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]dr\right\vert ^{2}dt \\ \leq & \; \frac{1}{R^{2}}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{t}^{T}|\widehat{c}(r,t)|^{2}drdt\cdot \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}[x_{i}(r)-\gamma\widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]^{2}dr. \end{align*} Hence $\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt$ is bounded, too. Then the desired result holds. \hfill
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to $L^2$ bounds on $x_i$ and $\widehat u_i$; bound $x^N$ via Lemma 3.2 applied to (6.10), then $x_i$ and $\widehat u_i$.

nodes.name: Unilateral deviation dynamics
nodes.definiendum: states under a unilateral deviation of player $\mathcal{A}_i$
nodes.statement_short: All players except $\mathcal{A}_i$ use the decentralized control while $\mathcal{A}_i$ uses an arbitrary control $u_i$.

nodes.name: Mean-field approximation under a unilateral deviation
nodes.statement: Suppose $\widehat{a}$ is the solution of NCE equation (\ref{3.14}), (\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for two cases of $A=\widehat{f}$, $B=\widehat{c}$ and $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c}$. Moreover, $(1+K_2)K_1\frac{360}{N^{2}R^2}L^2<\frac 1 2$, where \[ L=\int_0^T\int_0^t|\widehat{c}(t,s)|^2dsdt, \quad K_1=\int_0^T\int_0^t|\widehat{f}(t,s)|^2dsdt,\quad K_2=\int_0^T\int_0^t|P_0(t,s)|^2dsdt, \] $P_0$ is defined in (\ref{6.3}) with $A=\widehat{f}$. Then we have \begin{eqnarray*} \mathbb{E}\int_0^T|\widehat{a}(s)-x^{N}(s)|^2ds=O\Big(\frac{1}{N}\Big), \end{eqnarray*} where $x^{N}(t)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{l=1}^{N}x_{l}(t),$ $x_l$ satisfies (\ref{6.12}) and (\ref{6.13}).
assumptions: $\widehat{a}$ is the solution of NCE equation (\ref{3.14}),
(\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for two cases of $A=\widehat{f}$, $B=\widehat{c}$ and $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c}$.
conclusions: \mathbb{E}\int_0^T|\widehat{a}(s)-x^{N}(s)|^2ds=O\Big(\frac{1}{N}\Big),
nodes.statement_short: Even when one player deviates, the population average stays $O(1/N)$-close to $\widehat a$ in mean square.
nodes.label: lemma6.4

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.7
nodes.statement:
For convenience, we also rewrite (ef{6.13}) as  egin{align} x_{i}(t) = & \; \varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)x_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)\widehat{u}_{i}(s)ds 
onumber \ & +\int_{0}^{t}\sigma (t,s)dW_{i}(s)+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)[x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)]ds 
onumber \ & +\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)[u_{i}(s)-\widehat{u}_{i}(s)]ds, \end{align} where $\widehat{u}_i$ is defined as  egin{eqnarray} \widehat{u}_{i}(t)=- rac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\!\!\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)[x_{i}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]dr, \end{eqnarray} and $x_{i}$ satisfies (ef{6.13}). After some direct calculations,  egin{align*} x^{N}(t) = & \; \widehat{\varphi }(t)+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds+ rac{1}{N}\sum_{l=1}^{N}\widehat{\sigma }_{l}(t) \ & -\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s) rac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}s}\int_{s}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,s)[x^{N}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]drds \ & +\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)[x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)]ds+ rac{1}{N}\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)[u_{i}(s)-\widehat{u}_{i}(s)]ds, \end{align*} where $\widehat{\varphi}$, $\widehat{f}$, $\widehat{\sigma}_l$ are defined in (ef{3.8.1}). Using Fubini theorem, it also follows from (ef{3.9}) (with $a=\widehat{a}$) that  egin{align*} \overline{x}^{N}(t) = & \; \widehat{\varphi }(t)+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds+ rac{1}{N}\sum_{l=1}^{N}\widehat{\sigma }_{l}(t) \ & -\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s) rac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}s}\!\!\int_{s}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,s)[\overline{x}^{N}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]drds, \end{align*} therefore we have  egin{align} x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t) = & \; \overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)[x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)]ds 
onumber \ & -\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s) rac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}s}\!\!\int_{s}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,s)[x^{N}(r)-\widehat{a}(r)]drds 
onumber \ & +\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s) rac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}s}\!\!\int_{s}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,s)[\overline{x}^{N}(r)-\widehat{a}(r)]drds 
onumber \ & + rac{1}{N}\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)[u_{i}(s)-\widehat{u}_{i}(s)]ds. \end{align} Note that if $A=0$, $B=\widehat{c}$, then (ef{6.2}) and (ef{6.3}) imply $\overline{x}^N$ is bounded in $L^2_{\mathcal{F}}(0,T;\mathbb{R}).$ Similarly, if (ef{6.2}) and (ef{6.3}) hold with $A=\widehat{f}$, $B=\widehat{c}$, then using Lemma ef{lemma6-1} to (ef{6.16}), we have  egin{eqnarray} &&\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt 
onumber\ &&\leq (1+K_2)\left[(36+12R^2)\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt+ rac{36}{N^{2}}L\cdot \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}[u_{i}(s)-\widehat{u}_{i}(s)]^{2}dsight], \end{eqnarray} where $L$ and $K_2$ are defined before. On the other hand, from Lemma ef{lemma6.3}, $\mathcal{J}_i(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})$ is bounded, it then suffices to consider $u_i$ in (ef{6.13}) such that $\mathcal{J}_i(u_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})\leq \mathcal{J}_i(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})$, which implies that $\mathbb{E}\int_0^T|u_i(t)|^2dt\leq C$. As to $\widehat{u}_i$ in (ef{6.15}), we have  egin{align*} \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt = & \;  rac{1}{R^{2}}\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)[x_{i}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]dright\vert ^{2}dt \ \leq & \;  rac{1}{R^{2}}L\cdot \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}[x_{i}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]^{2}dr, \end{align*} therefore,  egin{align} \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}[u_{i}(s)-\widehat{u}_{i}(s)]^{2}ds \leq & \; 2\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|u_{i}(s)|^{2}ds+2\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(s)|^{2}ds 
onumber \ \leq & \; C+ rac{2}{R^{2}}L\cdot \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(r)|^{2}dr, \end{align} where $C$ does not depend on $N$. Substituting (ef{6.18}) into (ef{6.17}), we have  egin{eqnarray} &&\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt
onumber\ && \leq (1+K_2)(36+12R^2)\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt
onumber \ &&+ rac{C}{N^{2}}+ (1+K_2) rac{72}{N^{2}R^2}L^2\cdot \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}[u_{i}(s)-\widehat{u}_{i}(s)]^{2}ds. \end{eqnarray} After some transformations, we can rewrite (ef{6.13}) as  egin{align*} x_{i}(t) = & \; \widehat{\varphi }(t)+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)[x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)]ds \ & +\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)u_{i}(s)ds+\widehat{\sigma }_{i}(t), \end{align*} therefore,  egin{align} \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)|^{2}dt \leq & \; 5\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{\varphi }(t)|^{2}dt+5\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{t}|\widehat{f}(t,s)|^{2}dsdt\cdot\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)|^{2}ds 
onumber \ & +5\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{t}|\widehat{f}(t,s)|^2dsdt\cdot \int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{a}(s)|^{2}ds 
onumber \ & +5\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{t}|\widehat{c}(t,s)|^{2}dsdt\cdot\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|u_{i}(s)|^{2}ds+\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{\sigma}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt. \end{align} Since $\widehat{\varphi}$, $\widehat{f}$, $\widehat{a}$, $\sigma$ are bounded, substituting (ef{6.19}) into (ef{6.20}) yields  egin{eqnarray*} \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)|^{2}dt\leq C+C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{ x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt+ (1+K_2)K_1 rac{360}{N^{2}R^2}L^2\cdot \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}[x_{i}(s)]^{2}ds. \end{eqnarray*} So if $(1+K_2)K_1 rac{360}{N^{2}R^2}L^2< rac 1 2,$ then we have \[ \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)|^{2}dt\leq C+C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{x}^{N}(t)- \widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt, \] which implies the boundedness of $\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)|^{2}dt$. By combining (ef{6.19}), (ef{6.20}) and Lemma ef{lemma-2}, we obtained the desired result. \hfill
nodes.statement_short: Write $x^N-\widehat a$ as a solution of (6.1) with a $1/N$ deviation term and close the estimate on $\|x_i\|$ under the smallness condition. The key step is absorbing the $\|x_i\|^2$ term with coefficient below $1/2$.

nodes.name: Remark 3.3 (comparison with Lemma 3.4 and Nguyen-Huang)
nodes.statement: Compared with Lemma 3.4 above, our result here seems to be more general because $u_i$ in (\ref{6.13}) is not necessary to be $\widehat{u}_i$ in (\ref{3.18}). Moreover, our result also generalizes the corresponding result in \cite{N-H 2012} in that our state equation can degenerate to the linear SDEs there. In addition, our approach here is also different from the one used in \cite{N-H 2012}. At last, although the conditions imposed on above coefficients $K_1$, $K_2$ and $L$ seem to be technical, it has two interesting features. First, the above inequality holds true in general because $N$ is always sufficiently large. Second, such condition is not required in the nontrivial case $\widehat{f}=0.$

nodes.name: epsilon-Nash equilibrium of the decentralized controls
nodes.statement: Suppose $\varphi$, $f$, $b$ and $c$ are bounded and continuous in $t$, the NCE equation (\ref{3.14}) admits a unique continuous solution $\widehat{a}\in C[0,T]$. (\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold with $A=\widehat{f}$, $B=\widehat{c}$ and $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c}$. Moreover, $(1+K_2)K_1\frac{360}{N^{2}R^2}L^2<\frac 1 2$, where $L,\ K_1,\ K_2$ are defined in Lemma \ref{lemma6.4}. Then the set of control $\widehat{u}_i$ in (\ref{3.18}) with $1\leq i\leq N$ for $N$ players is an $\epsilon$-Nash equilibrium, i.e., for $1\leq i\leq N$, $$\mathcal{J}_i(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})-\epsilon\leq \inf\limits_{u_i\in L^2_{\mathcal{F}}[0,T]}\mathcal{J}_i(u_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})\leq \mathcal{J}_i(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i}). $$

(\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold with $A=\widehat{f}$, $B=\widehat{c}$ and $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c}$.
conclusions: the set of control $\widehat{u}_i$ in (\ref{3.18}) with $1\leq i\leq N$ for $N$ players is an $\epsilon$-Nash equilibrium
nodes.statement_short: The NCE-based decentralized controls form an $\epsilon$-Nash equilibrium with $\epsilon=O(1/\sqrt N)$.
nodes.label: theorem3.3

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.4
nodes.statement: If we denote by $\xi_a(t)=x^N(t)-\widehat{a}(t),$ $\xi_b(t)=\gamma(\widehat{a}(t)-x^N(t))$, then the dynamics and cost functional of $\mathcal{A}_i$ can be rewritten as \begin{align} x_{i}(t) = & \; \varphi(t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)x_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds \nonumber \\ & +\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)\xi_{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma(t,s)dW_{i}(s), \end{align} and \[ J_{i}(u_{i})=\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left[ |x_{i}(t)-\gamma\widehat{a}(t)-\eta +\xi _{b}(t)|^{2}+R|u_{i}(t)|^{2}\right]dt. \] From Lemma \ref{lemma6.4}, we have $\epsilon_a+\epsilon_b=O(\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}})$, and $\mathbb{E}\int_0^T|x_i(t)|^2dt+\mathbb{E}\int_0^T|u_i(t)|^2dt\leq C,$ where $C$ is independent of $N$, $\epsilon_a$, $\epsilon_b$ are defined in (\ref{6.6}), it then follows from Lemma \ref{lemma6.4}, Theorem \ref{theorem3.2} that \[ \mathcal{J}_i(u_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})\geq \overline{J}_i(\overline{u}_i)-O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}\right) \geq \mathcal{J}_i(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})-O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}\right). \] The conclusion is thus proved. \hfill
nodes.statement_short: View a deviation as a perturbed limiting problem with $\xi_a,\xi_b=O(1/\sqrt N)$ and combine Lemmas 3.5, 3.7 and Theorem 3.3.

nodes.statement:
In this case, $\varphi ,b,c,\sigma $ are independent of $t$, and
Equation (\ref{2.1}) becomes
\begin{eqnarray} x_{i}(t)=x(0)+\int_{0}^{t}b(s)x_{i}(s)ds+
\int_{0}^{t}c(s)u_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma(s)dW_i(s),
\end{eqnarray}

nodes.name: Resolvent and coefficients in the SDE case
nodes.statement:
For $s,t\in[0,T],$ we have

\[
\Lambda^{1}(s,t)=b(t), \quad
\Lambda^{k+1}(s,t)=b(t)\left(\int_{t}^{s}b(r)dr\right)^{k}, \quad
P(s,t)=b(t)e^{\int_{t}^{s}b(u)du}.
\]

Therefore,

\begin{eqnarray*}
& & \widehat{\varphi }(t) = x(0)e^{\int_{0}^{t}b(r)dr}, \quad \widehat{\sigma}_i(t) =\int_{0}^{t}\sigma (s)e^{\int_{s}^{t}b(r)dr}dW_{i}(s), \\
& & \widehat{c}(s,t)=c(t)e^{\int_{t}^{s}b(r)dr}, \quad M(t,s)=\int_{0}^{s\wedge t}|c(r)|^{2}e^{\int_{r}^{t}b(v)dv+\int_{r}^{s}b(v)dv}dr.
\end{eqnarray*}

nodes.name: Remark 4.1 (comparison with the Riccati approach)
nodes.statement: One can express $\widehat{u}_i$ in (\ref{4.3}) as $\widehat{u}_i(t)=\frac 1 R c(t)[-P'(t)x_i(t)+\delta(t)]$ where $P'$ and $\delta$ satisfy Riccati equation and backward ordinary differential equation respectively, see for example, \cite{H 2010}, \cite{H-C-M 2007} and \cite{N-H 2012}. Such procedure is different from ours here. More precise, it makes use the advantage of state equation and optimal control (note that $s$ and $t$ are separable). However, such skills are hard to be applied in more general model such as the state equations with delay below. In such sense, our approach applied here is more flexiable which can fill this technical gap.

nodes.name: Freeze the Fredholm term
nodes.statement: Given $y(\cdot )\in L_{\mathcal{F}}^{2}(0,T;\mathbb{R}),$ consider the following Volterra equation \begin{eqnarray} x(t)=\varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}A(t,s)x(s)ds-\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{s \wedge t}B(t,r)B(s,r)\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{r}}y(s)drds, \end{eqnarray} which obviously admits a unique solution $x(\cdot)$ under above assumptions.
nodes.statement_short: Fix $y$ and solve the resulting Volterra equation (6.5).

nodes.name: Resolvent rewriting
nodes.statement: By using Lemma 1.1 in \cite{Y 1996}, we can rewrite (\ref{6.5}) as \[ x(t)=\widehat{\varphi }(t)-\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{s\wedge t} \widehat{B}(t,r)B(s,r)\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{r}}y(s)drds. \]
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite (6.5) via the resolvent kernel $P_0$.

nodes.name: Contraction mapping
nodes.statement: Then using the idea of contraction mapping and Lemma \ref{lemma-1}, together with above requirements, we can obtain the existence of $x(\cdot)$ in $L_{\mathcal{F}}^{2}(0,T;\mathbb{R})$ satisfying (\ref{6.4}). \hfill
nodes.statement_short: Contraction mapping with Lemma 3.1 gives existence and (6.4).

nodes.name: Reduce to equation (6.1)
nodes.statement: From (\ref{3.14}) and (\ref{3.20}), we know the difference between $\overline{x}_i$ and $\widehat{a}$ satisfies the type of Equation (\ref{6.1}) with $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c}$, $\varphi=\widehat{\sigma}_i$.
nodes.statement_short: The difference $\overline x_i-\widehat a$ solves (6.1) with $A=0$, $B=\widehat c$.

nodes.name: Apply estimate (6.4)
nodes.statement: Then by means of (\ref{6.4}), \begin{eqnarray*} \mathbb{E}\int_0^T|\overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt &\leq &C\mathbb{E}\int_0^T\left\vert \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^{N}\widehat{\sigma }_{i}(t)\right\vert ^{2}dt. \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the averaged difference by the average of $\widehat\sigma_i$.

nodes.name: Independence gives O(1/N)
nodes.statement: It then follows from the boundedness of $\sigma$ and $P$ in (\ref{3.8.1}), together with the independence of $W_i$ ($i=1,2,\cdots,N$) that \[ \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt=O\left(\frac{1}{N}\right), \] which implies the desired result. \hfill
nodes.statement_short: Independence of the $W_i$ yields the $O(1/N)$ rate.

nodes.name: Rewrite x_i around x-bar_i
nodes.statement: Comparing (\ref{3.19}) and (\ref{3.20}), we can rewrite $x_i(t)$ as \begin{align*} x_i(t)=& \; \overline{x}_i(t)+\int_0^t\widehat{f}(t,s)\Big[x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)\Big]ds \\ &-\frac{1}{R}\int_0^T\int_0^{s\wedge t}\widehat{c}(t,r)\widehat{c}(s,r)\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_r}[x_i(s)-\overline{x}_i(s)]drds. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Express $x_i$ as $\overline x_i$ plus correction terms.

nodes.name: Equation for x^N - a-hat
nodes.statement: Therefore, \begin{align*} x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)=& \; \overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)+\int_0^t\widehat{f}(t,s)\Big[x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)\Big]ds\nonumber\\ & - \frac 1 R \int_0^T\int_0^{s\wedge t}\widehat{c}(t,r)\widehat{c}(s,r)\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_r}[x^N(s)-\widehat{a}(s)]drds\nonumber\\ &+\frac 1 R \int_0^T\int_0^{s\wedge t}\widehat{c}(t,r)\widehat{c}(s,r)\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_r}[\overline{x}^N(s)-\widehat{a}(s)]drds. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Average to get an equation of type (6.1) for $x^N-\widehat a$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemmas 3.2 and 3.3
nodes.statement: By using Lemma \ref{lemma6-1}, Lemma \ref{lemma-2}, together with the boundedness of $\widehat{f}$ and $\widehat{c}$, we can obtain the desired result (\ref{3.23}). \hfill
nodes.statement_short: Lemmas 3.2 and 3.3 give (3.23).

nodes.name: Expand cost difference
nodes.statement: First from the definition of $\mathcal{J}_i$ in (\ref{2.2}) and $\overline{J}_i$ in (\ref{3.2}), \begin{align*} \mathcal{J}_{i}(\widehat{u}_{i},\widehat{u}_{-i})-\overline{J}_{i}( \overline{u}_{i}) \leq & \; C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert R|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}-R|\overline{u} _{i}(t)|^{2}\right\vert dt \\ &+C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert |x_{i}(t)-\gamma x^{N}(t)-\eta |^{2}-|\overline{ x}_{i}(t)-\gamma \widehat{a}(t)-\eta |^{2}\right\vert dt \\ \leq & \; C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}R\left[ |\widehat{u}_{i}(t)-\overline{u} _{i}(t)|^{2}+2|\overline{u}_{i}(t)|\cdot|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)-\overline{u} _{i}(t)|\right] dt \\ &+C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)-\overline{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma (x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a} (t))|^{2}dt \\ &+C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma \widehat{a}(t)-\eta |\cdot |x_{i}(t)-\overline{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma (x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t))|dt, \end{align*} where $x_{i}$ and $\overline{x}_{i}$ satisfy (\ref{3.19}) and (\ref{3.20}) respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the cost difference by control and state difference terms.

nodes.name: Control difference bound
nodes.statement: It follows from (\ref{3.3}) and (\ref{3.18}) that \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)-\overline{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt \leq & \; \frac{1}{R^{2}}\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\left\vert \int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(s,t)[x_{i}(s)-\overline{x}_{i}(s)]ds\right\vert ^{2}dt \\ \leq & \; C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(s)-\overline{x}_{i}(s)|^{2}ds. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Control difference is controlled by state difference.

nodes.name: Boundedness of optimal state and control
nodes.statement: Note that equation (\ref{3.20}) is one special case of (\ref{6.1}) with $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c}$. Under above requirement, then from inequality (\ref{6.4}) above we have the boundedness of $\overline{x}_i$ in $L^2_{\mathcal{F}}(0,T;\mathbb{R})$. Recalling (\ref{3.6}) with $a=\widehat{a}$, we can also get similar boundedness result for $\overline{u}_i$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3.2 gives $L^2$ bounds on $\overline x_i$ and $\overline u_i$.

nodes.name: Schwarz bound on cross term
nodes.statement: As a result, by Schwarz's inequality, \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{u}_{i}(t)||\widehat{u}_{i}(t)-\overline{u}_{i}(t)|dt \leq & \left[ \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt\right] ^{\frac{1}{2}} \left[\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)-\overline{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt\right] ^{\frac{1}{2}} \\ \leq & \; C\left[ \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(s)-\overline{x}_{i}(s)|^{2}ds\right] ^{\frac{1}{2}}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Schwarz's inequality bounds the control cross term.

nodes.name: Split state difference
nodes.statement: On the other hand, \begin{eqnarray*} \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)-\overline{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma (x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t))|^{2}dt \leq C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)-\overline{x}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt+C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt. \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Split the state term into $x_i-\overline x_i$ and $x^N-\widehat a$.

nodes.name: Schwarz bound on state cross term
nodes.statement: Similarly, we can use Schwarz's inequality to estimate \begin{eqnarray*} &&\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma \widehat{a}(t)-\eta |\cdot |x_{i}(t)-\overline{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma (x^{(N)}(t)-\widehat{a}(t))|dt\\ &&\leq C\left[\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)-\overline{x}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt\right]^{\frac 1 2}+C\left[\mathbb{E} \int_{0}^{T}|x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt\right]^{\frac 1 2}. \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Schwarz's inequality bounds the state cross term.

nodes.name: Conclude by Lemma 3.4
nodes.statement: Therefore, by using Lemma \ref{lemma-3}, we obtain the desired result. \hfill
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3.4's $O(1/N)$ bounds give the $O(1/\sqrt N)$ rate.

nodes.name: Decompose control around optimal
nodes.statement: For convenience, we can rewrite (\ref{6.7}) as \begin{align*} x_{i}(t) = & \; \varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)x_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}^{\prime }(s)ds \\ &+\int_{0}^{t}g(t,s)\xi _{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)\overline{u}_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma (t,s)dW_{i}(s). \end{align*} Here $u_{i}^{\prime }(s)=u_{i}(s)-\overline{u}_{i}(s),$ \[ \overline{u}_{i}(s)=-\frac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c} (r,t)[x_{i}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]dr, \] where $x_{i}$ satisfies (\ref{6.7}), $\widehat{c}$ is given in (\ref{3.7}).
nodes.statement_short: Write $u_i=\overline u_i+u_i'$.

nodes.name: Bound on u'
nodes.statement: It then follows from inequality (\ref{6.8}) that $\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|u_{i}^{\prime }(t)|^{2}dt\leq C$.
nodes.statement_short: The deviation $u_i'$ is $L^2$-bounded.

nodes.name: Auxiliary control problem
nodes.statement: Next we construct one auxiliary optimal control problem with state equation and cost functional as \begin{align} \widetilde{x}_{i}(t) = & \; \varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)\widetilde{x}_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds \nonumber \\ &+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}''(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)\overline{u}_{i}(s,\widetilde{x}_{i})ds+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma (t,s)dW_{i}(s), \end{align} and \[ \widetilde{J}_{i}(u_{i}'')=\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left[|\widetilde{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma \widehat{a}(t)-\eta |^{2}+R|u_{i}''(t)+\overline{u}_{i}(t,\widetilde{x}_{i})|^{2}\right]dt. \] where $u''_{i}$ is the control variable. For $t\in[0,T]$, $\overline{u}_{i}(t,\widetilde{x}_{i})$ in (\ref{6.9}) is defined as \[ \overline{u}_{i}(t,\widetilde{x}_{i})=-\frac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\!\!\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)[\widetilde{x}_{i}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]dr. \] Obviously, $\widetilde{J}_{i}(u_{i}'')$ attains its minimum when $u_{i}''=0,$ and the corresponding cost functional equals to $ \overline{J}_{i}(\overline{u}_{i}).$
nodes.statement_short: Introduce an auxiliary problem whose minimum, at $u''=0$, equals $\overline J_i(\overline u_i)$.

nodes.name: Solve for M'
nodes.statement: On the other hand, by Lemma \ref{lemma6-1}, \[ M_{i}'(t)=\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}'(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)M_{i}'(s)ds-\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)M_{i}'(r)drds \] admits a unique solution $M_{i}'$ such that \[ \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|M_{i}^{\prime }(t)|^{2}dt\leq 6\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}'(s)ds\right\vert^{2}dt\leq C. \]
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3.2 gives a bounded solution $M_i'$.

nodes.name: Identify auxiliary state
nodes.statement: If we take $u_{i}''=u_{i}'(s)=u_{i}(s)-\overline{u}_{i}(s)$, and $\widetilde{x}_{i}'$ is the corresponding solution of (\ref{6.9}), then $\widetilde{x}_{i}'=\overline{x}_{i}(t)+M_{i}'(t),$ where $\overline{x}_{i}(t)$ is the optimal state in (\ref{3.9}) with $a=\widehat{a}$. Moreover, recalling the boundedness of $\overline{x}_i$ in $L^2_{\mathcal{F}}(0,T;\mathbb{R})$, we also have $\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widetilde{x}_{i}'(t)|^{2}dt\leq C$.
nodes.statement_short: With $u''=u'$ the auxiliary state is $\overline x_i+M_i'$, bounded in $L^2$.

nodes.name: Compare perturbed and auxiliary states
nodes.statement: Since $x_{i}$ and $\widetilde{x}_{i}'$ are given in (\ref{6.7}) and (\ref{6.9}), thus their difference $d_{i}=x_{i}-\widetilde{x}_{i}'$ satisfy \[ d_{i}(t)=\int_{0}^{t}g(t,s)\xi _{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)d_{i}(s)ds-\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\!\!\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)d_{i}(r)drds. \] Under above requirements, from Lemma \ref{lemma6-1}, we have \[ \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)-\widetilde{x}_{i}^{\prime }(t)|^{2}dt\leq 6\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert\int_{0}^{t}g(t,s)\xi _{a}(s)ds\right\vert^{2}dt\leq C\epsilon _{a}^{2}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3.2 bounds $x_i-\widetilde x_i'$ by $C\epsilon_a^2$.

nodes.name: Cost difference estimate
nodes.statement: Following the similar arguments in \cite{N-H 2012}, we should have \[ |J_{i}^{\xi}(u_{i})-\widetilde{J}_{i}(u_{i}')| \leq C(1+\epsilon_b)(\epsilon _{a}+\epsilon _{b}), \] where $C$ does not depend on $\xi_a$ and $\xi_b$.
nodes.statement_short: As in Nguyen-Huang, the cost difference is $O((1+\epsilon_b)(\epsilon_a+\epsilon_b))$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: After combining the estimate of $\widetilde{J}_{i}(u_{i}')\geq \overline{J}_i(\overline{u}_i)$, we can get the desired result. \hfill
nodes.statement_short: Combine with the optimality of the auxiliary problem.

nodes.name: Reduce to L2 bounds
nodes.statement: If we can prove \[ \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(s)|^{2}ds\leq C,\quad \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(s)|^{2}ds\leq C, \] where $x_i$ satisfies (\ref{3.19}), $C$ does not depend on $N,$ then the result holds directly.
nodes.statement_short: It suffices to bound $\widehat u_i$ and $x_i$ in $L^2$ uniformly in $N$.

nodes.name: Equation for x^N
nodes.statement: From (\ref{3.19}), we have \begin{align} x^{N}(t) = & \; \widehat{\varphi }(t)+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)x^{N}(s)ds+\frac{1}{N}\sum_{l=1}^{N}\widehat{\sigma }_{l}(t) \nonumber \\ &-\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)\frac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}s}\int_{s}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,s)[x^{N}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]drds, \end{align} where $x^{N}(t)=\frac{1}{N}\sum\limits_{l=1}^{N}x_{l}(t).$
nodes.statement_short: Average (3.19) to get (6.10).

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 3.2 to x^N
nodes.statement: Note that (\ref{6.10}) is one special case of equation (\ref{6.1}), (\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for $A=\widehat{f}$, $B=\widehat{c}$, it then follows from Lemma \ref{lemma6-1} that \begin{align} \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x^{N}(s)|^{2}ds \leq & \; C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{\varphi}(s)|^{2}ds+C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert \frac{1}{N}\sum_{l=1}^{N}\widehat{\sigma}_{l}(t)\right\vert ^{2}dt \nonumber \\ & +C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{a}(s)|^{2}ds+C. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3.2 yields the bound (6.11).

nodes.name: Bound x_i
nodes.statement: As to $x_i$ in equation (\ref{3.19}), using (\ref{6.11}) and conditions (\ref{6.2}), (\ref{6.3}) with $A=0$, $B=\widehat{c}$, we should have $\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(s)|^{2}ds\leq C$ where $C$ is independent of $N$.
nodes.statement_short: Deduce an $N$-uniform bound on $x_i$.

nodes.name: Bound the control
nodes.statement: At last, we know that \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt = & \; \frac{1}{R^{2}}\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)[x_{i}(r)-\gamma\widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]dr\right\vert ^{2}dt \\ \leq & \; \frac{1}{R^{2}}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{t}^{T}|\widehat{c}(r,t)|^{2}drdt\cdot \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}[x_{i}(r)-\gamma\widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]^{2}dr. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\widehat u_i$ in terms of $x_i$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Hence $\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt$ is bounded, too. Then the desired result holds. \hfill
nodes.statement_short: Hence the cost is bounded.

nodes.name: Rewrite deviating dynamics
nodes.statement: For convenience, we also rewrite (\ref{6.13}) as \begin{align} x_{i}(t) = & \; \varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)x_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)\widehat{u}_{i}(s)ds \nonumber \\ & +\int_{0}^{t}\sigma (t,s)dW_{i}(s)+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)[x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)]ds \nonumber \\ & +\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)[u_{i}(s)-\widehat{u}_{i}(s)]ds, \end{align} where $\widehat{u}_i$ is defined as \begin{eqnarray} \widehat{u}_{i}(t)=-\frac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\!\!\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)[x_{i}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]dr, \end{eqnarray} and $x_{i}$ satisfies (\ref{6.13}).
nodes.statement_short: Write the deviating dynamics around $\widehat u_i$ and $\widehat a$.

nodes.name: Equation for x^N
nodes.statement: After some direct calculations, \begin{align*} x^{N}(t) = & \; \widehat{\varphi }(t)+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds+\frac{1}{N}\sum_{l=1}^{N}\widehat{\sigma }_{l}(t) \\ & -\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)\frac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}s}\int_{s}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,s)[x^{N}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]drds \\ & +\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)[x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)]ds+\frac{1}{N}\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)[u_{i}(s)-\widehat{u}_{i}(s)]ds, \end{align*} where $\widehat{\varphi}$, $\widehat{f}$, $\widehat{\sigma}_l$ are defined in (\ref{3.8.1}).
nodes.statement_short: Compute the equation of the state average.

nodes.name: Difference equation (6.16)
nodes.statement:
Using Fubini theorem, it also follows from (ef{3.9}) (with $a=\widehat{a}$) that  egin{align*} \overline{x}^{N}(t) = & \; \widehat{\varphi }(t)+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds+ rac{1}{N}\sum_{l=1}^{N}\widehat{\sigma }_{l}(t) \ & -\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s) rac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}s}\!\!\int_{s}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,s)[\overline{x}^{N}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]drds, \end{align*} therefore we have  egin{align} x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t) = & \; \overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)[x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)]ds 
onumber \ & -\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s) rac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}s}\!\!\int_{s}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,s)[x^{N}(r)-\widehat{a}(r)]drds 
onumber \ & +\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s) rac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}s}\!\!\int_{s}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,s)[\overline{x}^{N}(r)-\widehat{a}(r)]drds 
onumber \ & + rac{1}{N}\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)[u_{i}(s)-\widehat{u}_{i}(s)]ds. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Subtract the equation for $\overline x^N$ to get (6.16).

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 3.2 to (6.16)
nodes.statement: Note that if $A=0$, $B=\widehat{c}$, then (\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) imply $\overline{x}^N$ is bounded in $L^2_{\mathcal{F}}(0,T;\mathbb{R}).$ Similarly, if (\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold with $A=\widehat{f}$, $B=\widehat{c}$, then using Lemma \ref{lemma6-1} to (\ref{6.16}), we have \begin{eqnarray} &&\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt \nonumber\\ &&\leq (1+K_2)\left[(36+12R^2)\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt+\frac{36}{N^{2}}L\cdot \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}[u_{i}(s)-\widehat{u}_{i}(s)]^{2}ds\right], \end{eqnarray} where $L$ and $K_2$ are defined before.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3.2 gives estimate (6.17).

nodes.name: Restrict to cost-improving deviations
nodes.statement: On the other hand, from Lemma \ref{lemma6.3}, $\mathcal{J}_i(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})$ is bounded, it then suffices to consider $u_i$ in (\ref{6.13}) such that $\mathcal{J}_i(u_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})\leq \mathcal{J}_i(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})$, which implies that $\mathbb{E}\int_0^T|u_i(t)|^2dt\leq C$.
nodes.statement_short: By Lemma 3.6 it suffices to consider $u_i$ with bounded $L^2$ norm.

nodes.name: Control difference bound
nodes.statement: As to $\widehat{u}_i$ in (\ref{6.15}), we have \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt = & \; \frac{1}{R^{2}}\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)[x_{i}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]dr\right\vert ^{2}dt \\ \leq & \; \frac{1}{R^{2}}L\cdot \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}[x_{i}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]^{2}dr, \end{align*} therefore, \begin{align} \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}[u_{i}(s)-\widehat{u}_{i}(s)]^{2}ds \leq & \; 2\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|u_{i}(s)|^{2}ds+2\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(s)|^{2}ds \nonumber \\ \leq & \; C+\frac{2}{R^{2}}L\cdot \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(r)|^{2}dr, \end{align} where $C$ does not depend on $N$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $u_i-\widehat u_i$ by $\|x_i\|$, giving (6.18).

nodes.name: Combine into (6.19)
nodes.statement: Substituting (\ref{6.18}) into (\ref{6.17}), we have \begin{eqnarray} &&\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt\nonumber\\ && \leq (1+K_2)(36+12R^2)\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt\nonumber \\ &&+\frac{C}{N^{2}}+ (1+K_2)\frac{72}{N^{2}R^2}L^2\cdot \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}[u_{i}(s)-\widehat{u}_{i}(s)]^{2}ds. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Substitute (6.18) into (6.17).

nodes.name: Bound x_i (6.20)
nodes.statement: After some transformations, we can rewrite (\ref{6.13}) as \begin{align*} x_{i}(t) = & \; \widehat{\varphi }(t)+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)[x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)]ds \\ & +\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)u_{i}(s)ds+\widehat{\sigma }_{i}(t), \end{align*} therefore, \begin{align} \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)|^{2}dt \leq & \; 5\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{\varphi }(t)|^{2}dt+5\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{t}|\widehat{f}(t,s)|^{2}dsdt\cdot\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)|^{2}ds \nonumber \\ & +5\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{t}|\widehat{f}(t,s)|^2dsdt\cdot \int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{a}(s)|^{2}ds \nonumber \\ & +5\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{t}|\widehat{c}(t,s)|^{2}dsdt\cdot\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|u_{i}(s)|^{2}ds+\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{\sigma}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the deviating state and bound it, giving (6.20).

nodes.name: Self-referential bound on x_i
nodes.statement: Since $\widehat{\varphi}$, $\widehat{f}$, $\widehat{a}$, $\sigma$ are bounded, substituting (\ref{6.19}) into (\ref{6.20}) yields \begin{eqnarray*} \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)|^{2}dt\leq C+C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{ x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt+ (1+K_2)K_1\frac{360}{N^{2}R^2}L^2\cdot \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}[x_{i}(s)]^{2}ds. \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Substitute (6.19) into (6.20).

nodes.name: Absorb under smallness
nodes.statement: So if $(1+K_2)K_1\frac{360}{N^{2}R^2}L^2<\frac 1 2,$ then we have \[ \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)|^{2}dt\leq C+C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{x}^{N}(t)- \widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt, \] which implies the boundedness of $\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)|^{2}dt$.
nodes.statement_short: Under the smallness condition, absorb the $\|x_i\|^2$ term.

nodes.name: Conclude by Lemma 3.3
nodes.statement: By combining (\ref{6.19}), (\ref{6.20}) and Lemma \ref{lemma-2}, we obtained the desired result. \hfill
nodes.statement_short: Combine with Lemma 3.3 to get $O(1/N)$.

nodes.name: Recast as perturbed problem
nodes.statement: If we denote by $\xi_a(t)=x^N(t)-\widehat{a}(t),$ $\xi_b(t)=\gamma(\widehat{a}(t)-x^N(t))$, then the dynamics and cost functional of $\mathcal{A}_i$ can be rewritten as \begin{align} x_{i}(t) = & \; \varphi(t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)x_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds \nonumber \\ & +\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)\xi_{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma(t,s)dW_{i}(s), \end{align} and \[ J_{i}(u_{i})=\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left[ |x_{i}(t)-\gamma\widehat{a}(t)-\eta +\xi _{b}(t)|^{2}+R|u_{i}(t)|^{2}\right]dt. \]
nodes.statement_short: Set $\xi_a=x^N-\widehat a$, $\xi_b=\gamma(\widehat a-x^N)$ to recast the deviation as the perturbed problem.

nodes.name: Combine estimates
nodes.statement: From Lemma \ref{lemma6.4}, we have $\epsilon_a+\epsilon_b=O(\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}})$, and $\mathbb{E}\int_0^T|x_i(t)|^2dt+\mathbb{E}\int_0^T|u_i(t)|^2dt\leq C,$ where $C$ is independent of $N$, $\epsilon_a$, $\epsilon_b$ are defined in (\ref{6.6}), it then follows from Lemma \ref{lemma6.4}, Theorem \ref{theorem3.2} that \[ \mathcal{J}_i(u_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})\geq \overline{J}_i(\overline{u}_i)-O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}\right) \geq \mathcal{J}_i(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})-O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}\right). \] The conclusion is thus proved. \hfill
